newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SHOCK DEFEAT PUTS ROBSON FUTURE IN DOUBT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOCK DEFEAT PUTS ROBSON FUTURE IN DOUBT.

text.p: Barcelona's shock defeat at home to struggling Hercules has prompted renewed rumours that coach Bobby Robson may be close to replacing Kevin Keegan at Newcastle United.
The vacant post will now be filled by either Robson or former Liverpool and Blackburn boss Kenny Dalglish with an announcement expected either on Tuesday or Wednesday.

Amid widespread media reports of the imminent arrival in Barcelona of Newcastle chairman Sir John Hall, there are also suggestions that Robson will demand a guarantee that he will complete his two-year contract at the Spanish club.
"If (Barcelona president) Jose Luis Nunez doesn't assure his continuity until '98 he could accept the Newcastle offer," read a headline in Tuesday's Barcelona daily 'El Mundo Deportivo'.
But another Spanish sports daily, 'Marca', warned that Robson may be contractually bound to pay Barcelona 600 million pesetas ($4.58 million) if he leaves without the club's consent.
Nunez is thought to have talked to the players and coaching staff after Monday's 3-2 defeat, which had begun with Barcelona storming to a 2-0 lead in just 15 minutes.
"We played a very good 30 minutes, perhaps our best of the season, and we could have got to three or four-nil," said Robson. "But games last 90 minutes."
Former England manager Robson said that Nunez had "hardly said anything" to him.
For Barcelona, the most positive note of the evening was struck by Brazilian striker Ronaldo, who broke a 56-day goal-drought to find the back of the net for the 14th time this season.
Barcelona now travel to fourth-placed Real Betis in a weekend of league action which could prove decisive.
Leaders Real Madrid face local rivals Atletico, the defending champions. Atletico, the most in-form team in country, are currently fifth.
